evidence.claim: Mosaic's 2025 10-K states phosphate operating results were unfavorably impacted by higher raw material costs, primarily sulfur.

Mosaic filings state it uses molten sulfur at phosphate concentrates plants to produce sulfuric acid, primarily for P2O5 production, and purchases most sulfur from North American oil and gas refiners.

memory_update.text: ECVT is the strongest underfollowed US-listed direct exposure found for the sulphuric-acid node because its disclosed business is virgin and regenerated sulfuric-acid products and services.
HWKN should remain in Layer 1 as a hypothesis-only distributor candidate until filings confirm whether sulfuric acid is financially material and whether tight acid markets can affect margins.
TGB is not a beneficiary by default; it is a hidden acid-dependent copper SX/EW user. Its 2026 fixed-price acid contract is a near-term mitigant but creates a post-2026 verification item.

MOS is a reference user rather than obscure discovery: sulfur is a primary cost input for phosphate production, so sulfur shocks can be visible through phosphate gross margin and sulfur consumed price.

Need another pass for US-listed or ADR smelter-acid byproduct producers, sulfur logistics/barge operators, refinery sulfur producers, and non-US listed Japanese/Korean smelter acid exporters that may be closer beneficiaries of the Kpler-described replacement trade routes.

node: Sulphur and sulphuric acid feedstock chokepoint for copper, nickel, fertilizers, and industrial acid
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint with a bias toward underfollowed suppliers, distributors, and second-order exposed users. The cleanest underfollowed supplier/regeneration exposure found is Ecovyst. Hawkins is a lower-confidence chemical distribution candidate. Taseko is a hidden acid-dependent copper SX/EW user with near-term contract protection. Mosaic is a more visible fertilizer reference name whose phosphate economics are directly exposed to sulfur and sulfuric-acid costs.
